findings: The review was performed against a git-archive snapshot of immutable implementation 3fb74a8bf518a528e89686d1390c223983fc98fb, with only the five fresh review-6 state-arrow perturbation pairs copied into that snapshot. The shared worktree's unrelated crates/rustuml-render/src/class.rs modification was excluded from validation.

Java provenance still supports the ordinary shared-arrow model. SkinParam.setParam cleans every key before map storage and style conversion; cleanForKeySlow lowercases, strips underscores and dots, rewrites activity/class/component/object/sequence/state/usecase Arrow prefixes to the shared arrow prefix, and FromSkinparamToStyle maps arrowColor to the arrow LineColor style.

Rust commit 3fb74a8b implements the corresponding ordinary storage boundary in parse::collapse_reassigned_skinparams: ordinary declarations compare through canonical_skinparam_key, and the arrowcolor identity is stored as the shared arrowcolor key. Synthetic theme body records remain keyed by theme segment plus raw lowercase key, preserving family scope for theme-expanded compatibility records.

StateSkin::from_diagram consumes the shared ordinary ArrowColor/stateArrowColor record after parser canonicalization, resolves stateBorderColor through the sibling state-border channel, and applies per-transition colour/style after the diagram-level arrow value. Static source inspection found no fixture labels, golden reads, SVG surgery, coordinate-keyed branches, or new unexplained constants in the reviewed implementation.

Four fresh state-only no-oracle perturbations passed strict comparison. They cover all seven family aliases, separator and case variants, alternating repeated keys, stateBorderColor interleaving, renamed states, varied chain lengths, and dashed/dotted local overrides.

The real repeated-theme state perturbation rejects acceptance under the strict no-oracle gate. The arrow-specific attributes match Java: inherited links use #2E7D32 after the final UseCase alias, and the local bold link uses #C2185B. The strict diff is instead dominated by broader themed state rendering: canvas dimensions, state-box height/width, pseudo-state coordinates, link geometry, and label coordinates.

The aggregate parity_perturbations run at the exact snapshot remains red. Besides the new review-6 repeated-theme state failure, it also reports pre-existing state-arrow themed heldouts checker_theme_user_order_and_local_override and review4_repeated_themes_bidirectional_order, plus preserved state-recursive-group-simplification failures. These failures mean the mechanism cannot be accepted by T14's no-oracle perturbation rule yet.

The frozen/mechanical guards passed individually: no golden data is embedded in shipping crates, the error-golden census guard skipped only because the archived snapshot has no populated golden submodule, decimal literals and comparator constants remain frozen, and parity review paths reject traversal.

Verdict is rejected. The ordinary alias/border/local-override model appears correct for non-themed state perturbations and for arrow attributes inside the themed perturbation, but latest acceptance would be false while the strict no-oracle perturbation gate remains red.
